s1.syndrome_frame: Painless testicular swelling with associated epididymal involvement and adrenal gland abnormalities
salient_findings: Enlargement and inhomogeneity of the right testis and epididymis
key_facts: 82-year-old man
Painless right testicular swelling of several weeks’ duration
No systemic symptoms
History of glaucoma, prostatic adenomectomy, and hernioplasty
Medications: dorzolamide, lansoprazole, and dutasteride
Testicular ultrasound showed enlargement and inhomogeneity of the right testis and epididymis
Ipsilateral hydrocele
Swelling persisted after 10 days of amoxicillin–clavulanate
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT confirmed testicular pathology
Bilateral macronodular adrenal enlargement
Adrenal nodules were absent on a CT scan 3 years earlier
18 FDG PET/CT showed intense uptake in the right testis
No uptake in the adrenal glands
Normal laboratory evaluation
Negative serologies for active HCV and EBV
Positive for past EBV

shortlist.label: Leydig cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Painless testicular swelling and intense uptake on 18 FDG PET/CT

shortlist.label: Seminoma
shortlist.why_kept: Painless testicular swelling and testicular ultrasound findings

shortlist.label: Adrenal metastasis from testicular cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral macronodular adrenal enlargement and testicular pathology

shortlist.label: Testicular cancer with adrenal metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: Testicular and adrenal gland abnormalities with intense uptake on 18 FDG PET/CT

raw.rationale: The patient's testicular ultrasound and CT scans show testicular pathology, and the 18 FDG PET/CT scan shows intense uptake in the right testis, indicating a primary testicular tumor. The bilateral macronodular adrenal enlargement with homogeneous attenuation, which was absent on a previous CT scan, suggests metastasis from the testicular cancer.

rejected.label: Leydig cell tumor
rejected.why: While possible, Leydig cell tumors are less common and the presence of adrenal metastasis is more suggestive of a testicular cancer with metastasis.

rejected.label: Testicular lymphoma
rejected.why: Testicular lymphoma is more common in older men, but the presence of adrenal metastasis and the intense uptake on the 18 FDG PET/CT scan is more indicative of a primary testicular cancer with metastasis.

rejected.label: Seminoma
rejected.why: Seminoma is a type of testicular cancer, but the presence of adrenal metastasis and the patient's age make testicular cancer with adrenal metastasis a more comprehensive diagnosis.

rejected.label: Adrenal metastasis from testicular cancer
rejected.why: This option is very similar to the chosen champion, but 'Testicular cancer with adrenal metastasis' better explains the primary testicular tumor and the metastasis to the adrenal glands.
